recommendations.regimenLabel: Remission induction — cyclophosphamide OR rituximab + glucocorticoids
steps: Assess for organ/life-threatening features (alveolar haemorrhage, active glomerulonephritis — always classed as severe even with normal renal function).
Induce remission of severe ANCA-associated vasculitis with cyclophosphamide OR rituximab plus glucocorticoids; consider adjunctive avacopan to reduce steroid exposure.

Reserve plasma exchange for selected cases (concurrent anti-GBM antibody, or controversial use in the most fulminant disease) — a large RCT showed no benefit on the ESRD/death composite, so it is not routine.
Confirm with ANCA and tissue biopsy; exclude infection/mimics before immunosuppression (a rising ANCA alone is not a reason to escalate therapy).
Maintenance immunosuppression after induction; give Pneumocystis (TMP-SMX) prophylaxis plus bone/gastric protection on glucocorticoids.

drugRefs.dose: 1 mg/kg/day (max ~60–80 mg), then tapered (IV methylprednisolone pulses, e.g. 500 mg–1 g/day for 1–3 days, in organ-threatening disease)
drugRefs.why: Rapidly suppresses inflammation; the backbone of remission induction combined with a steroid-sparing agent. Reduced-dose regimens (PEXIVAS) lower infection risk.

drugRefs.dose: 375 mg/m² weekly for 4 weeks (or 1 g on days 0 and 14)
drugRefs.why: Non-inferior to cyclophosphamide for induction (RAVE/RITUXVAS) and preferred for relapsing disease and where fertility preservation matters.

drugRefs.dose: IV pulse 15 mg/kg (max 1.2 g) every 2–3 weeks, or oral 2 mg/kg/day
drugRefs.freq: pulsed (2–3 weekly) or daily oral, adjusted for age/renal function
drugRefs.why: Alternative induction agent for severe ANCA-associated vasculitis; dose-reduce for renal impairment and older age. Give with mesna/hydration for bladder protection.
Adjunct that allows substantial reduction in glucocorticoid exposure while maintaining remission (ADVOCATE trial).

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — The Vasculitis Syndromes
EULAR Recommendations for the Management of ANCA-Associated Vasculitis (2022)
KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of ANCA-Associated Vasculitis (2024)

drugRefs.dose: 960 mg three times weekly (or 480 mg once daily)
drugRefs.why: Prevents Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia during high-dose glucocorticoid/immunosuppressive therapy; combine with bone and gastric protection.

refs: EULAR Recommendations for the Management of ANCA-Associated Vasculitis (2022)

confirm: Multisystem illness — purpura, mononeuritis, renal/lung involvement, raised inflammatory markers; ANCA and biopsy guide diagnosis.
